text: I bought the Tablet Pro Pen Tool from the MS Store, which adds a few options, though none that are useful to me. The net result is that I don't use the pen.I bought the stock Microsoft type cover and I was going to buy the MS pen, too. Because there were multiple options for each I did a little research and discovered that while all the aftermarket keyboards have serious drawbacks, most people seem to like this pen better than the MS pen. And it does have very nice feel for drawing and inking.My expectation for a pen comes from Wacom products, which are much more open in what you can assign. I was amazed that you can't even assign your own keystrokes - even with the aftermarket app. And really I expect keystrokes, macros, and system functions at minimum.Is this pen good compared with the MS pen: it seems that it is. Is this pen good compared to what I expected: it's literally useless for me apart from photography.I wanted to use this for annotating PDFs as I read. With no possibility of assigning my own keystrokes for the buttons it is it's easier to just use my finger.So I would recommend skipping a pen altogether unless you really need to do visual art on your Surface.

I’ve not used my vacuum once. I sweep up the big stuff and mop away. It picks up all the pet hair and debris I miss sweeping. This morning as I started my Saturday cleaning I decided to give it a whirl cleaning my walls. I popped on a new mop, made my mixture and...Oh my!!!! Who knew??? Next up is my white kitchen cabinets. This thing is awesome!!!

title: There's a trick to putting this together
text: I bought the three shelf 30" high by 24" wide shelf system.I watched some videos and the reviewers and company leave you to believe this must snap together when installing. This is not true. The pipe is too wide. The best you can achieve is grooves are almost in place.The real snap occurs when aligning one side with the groove on the pipe with a ridge inside the plastic fastener. Then add the other side and push as tight as you can. There will be a gap. When you bring the shelf down it will force the plastic fasteners tighter. But beware. The fasteners might come uncoupled or slide down the pipe.I wound up with three sides fitting and the fourth side misaligned because it slid down or came apart. Then I had to pull the shelf up above the other three sides and refasten the black sheet fastener, then push the shelf down. This happened three times on shelves before I got the hang of it.It would have been easier if the fasteners snapped shut over the pipe, but this did not happen for me. I've read other people complaining about this, and I anticipated it may happen. Glad I was able to sort it out though because the shelf system fits perfectly in my pantry and takes a lot of clutter off the floor.Still, only 3 stars for assembly, but four stars for the shelf system itself.

title: LOVE these
text: I absolutely love these. I am extremely organized and pretty much label everything. When we got a new desktop computer with new speakers and new webcam, there were cords going all over the place! These labels were recommended to me by someone, so I ended up purchasing them... And I was NOT disappointed. Super easy to use and there are a LOT of them. Plus, I like that they give you 5 different colors. The labels stick on the tabs just fine and the tabs themselves seem quite sturdy. Not only did I label all the cords running underneath the computer, but I also labeled everyone's phone chargers, the camera charger cords, and the wireless headphone charger. My dad saw what I had done (my masterpiece) and quickly bought some for himself so he could label his thousands of Christmas lights & cords... Really, they can be used to label pretty much anything. (Keep in mind that the tabs are zip-ties, so you can label anything that can be zip-tied.) I would highly recommend these to anyone!
